extracted.intended_audience: archives, libraries, cultural organizations, community groups, and leaders/scholars/librarians/archivists seeking Mellon Foundation Public Knowledge funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines describing the Mellon Foundation's Public Knowledge grant program: the kinds of organizations and projects supported (preservation, access, infrastructure), the program values, and the typical invite-driven application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus: preserving and making knowledge accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Public Knowledge grants support the work of the institutions and community groups that strengthen our cultural record by preserving, recording, organizing, and making knowledge accessible to the public in libraries, archives, and other settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should engage in activities that collect, preserve, and share knowledge so that it survives and remains available to the public; emphasis on tangible work in libraries, archives, and comparable settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient type: Archives and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Archives and libraries engaged in creating, preserving, and making accessible cultural and scholarly records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and projects based in archives and libraries that directly support preservation and access are primary candidates for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient type: Organizations addressing historical record gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations working to address gaps in the historical record and to increase public access to knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that identifies and remediates omissions or silences in historical/cultural records and improves public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient type: Collaborative technology and infrastructure projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative projects focused on creating and sustaining technology and infrastructure to preserve and share knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports collaborative efforts (likely multi-institutional) that build or maintain tools, platforms, or infrastructure necessary for long-term preservation and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/forms of knowledge supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is passed on through writing, photographs, audio, and emerging forms; knowledge is pervasive—but fragile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may involve traditional and emerging media; proposers should account for the particular preservation and access needs of the media they work with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value orientation: knowledge as public and social good
rubrics_metrics.description: For me, public knowledge means ensuring that knowledge access and production are treated as public and social goods ... for purposes that matter to people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should treat access and production of knowledge as serving the public interest and meaningful community purposes rather than narrow private aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended impact: build an informed, engaged, and fair society
rubrics_metrics.description: Through this work, we can build a more informed, engaged, and fair society—and ensure that vital voices and stories endure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how the work contributes to societal goals (informed public, engagement, equity) and the durability of underrepresented voices/stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection/process note: invitation-driven grantmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Our staff seek out and get to know innovative leaders, scholars, librarians, archivists, and culture bearers before inviting them to submit a proposal for funding. Most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most funding is by invitation; prospective applicants should be aware that unsolicited proposals may be less typical and that building relationships with program staff is a common pathway to invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who we support: knowledge bearers creating public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: We support the work of knowledge bearers who are creating an informed and engaged society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on centering practitioners ('knowledge bearers') whose work produces public value; projects should be grounded in communities and practitioners who steward cultural knowledge.
